# Unit tests for safeagents itself. Harness end-to-end tests live in tests/harnesses
# and run in their own harness-*.yml workflows.
name: tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  pytest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - name: Install safeagents
        run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: uv run pytest --ignore=tests/harnesses -v

# Using safeagents with coding agents

For every command and option, see [commands.md](commands.md).

Each page below shows how to put safeagents between one agent harness and its model server. They cover the 12 coding agents tracked by [Harness Lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ybelkada/harness-lens), plus Mistral Vibe.

safeagents checks tool calls in **OpenAI Chat Completions** and **Anthropic Messages** traffic. Every guide follows the same three steps:

1. Start `safeagents <the model server the harness normally uses>`.
2. Set the harness's base URL to `http://127.0.0.1:8787`, with or without `/v1` depending on the harness.
3. Make sure every model the harness uses goes through the proxy, including the ones for titles, summaries, compaction and subagents.

Harnesses that only speak the OpenAI Responses API or the Gemini API can be routed through the proxy, but their tool calls aren't checked yet.

| # | Harness | Protocol through safeagents | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [OpenClaw](openclaw.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | supported |
| 2 | [DeepSeek Harness](deepseek-harness.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | supported (API key) |
| 3 | [Hermes Agent](hermes-agent.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | supported |
| 4 | [OpenCode](opencode.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | supported |
| 5 | [GitHub Copilot (VS Code)](copilot-vscode.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | BYOK models only |
| 6 | [Claude Code](claude-code.md) | Anthropic Messages | supported |
| 7 | [Codex CLI](codex.md) | Responses API only | not supported yet |
| 8 | [pi](pi.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | supported |
| 9 | [Gemini CLI](gemini-cli.md) | Gemini API only | not supported |
| 10 | [Cline](cline.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions | supported |
| 11 | [OpenHands](openhands.md) | Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions (`api_mode="chat"`) | supported |
| 12 | [Qwen Code](qwen-code.md) | Chat Completions (Anthropic Messages via bearer-auth gateways) | supported |
| 13 | [Mistral Vibe](mistral-vibe.md) | Chat Completions (Mistral backend), Anthropic Messages | supported |

Each page names the harness version it was checked against. The guides come from reading each harness's documentation and source code at that version.

The guides for **pi, Claude Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code, OpenHands, DeepSeek Harness and Mistral Vibe** are also tested end to end in CI (`.github/workflows/harness-*.yml`). Each test runs the real harness, set up as its page describes, through safeagents against a scripted model (`tests/harnesses/`). It checks that flagged calls are blocked and never run, and that clean calls run. The other guides haven't been run, so start with `--log-only` and watch the proxy's terminal before you turn blocking on.

"""Shows reviewed tool calls in the terminal.

On a terminal: a boxed histogram of verdicts above a box of the latest calls, redrawn
in place. Piped: one plain line per call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections import Counter, deque
from typing import Self

from rich import box
from rich.console import Console, Group
from rich.live import Live
from rich.panel import Panel
from rich.table import Table
from rich.text import Text

from .constants import STATS_HEIGHT, VERDICTS
from .utils import summary


class Monitor:
    """Counts requests and calls and shows each call as it is reviewed."""

    def __init__(self, console: Console | None = None, setup: str = "") -> None:
        self.console = console or Console(stderr=True)
        self.counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
        self.setup = setup
        self.recent: deque[tuple[str, str, str, str, str, str]] = deque(maxlen=200)
        self._live = None
        if self.console.is_terminal:
            self._live = Live(self.render(), console=self.console, auto_refresh=False)

    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
        if self._live:
            self._live.start()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        if self._live:
            self._live.stop()

    def request(self) -> None:
        self.counts["requests"] += 1
        self._refresh()

    def record(
        self,
        tool: str,
        args: str,
        verdict: str,
        reason: str | None,
        signals: list[str],
        judge: str | None,
        call_id: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.counts["calls"] += 1
        self.counts[verdict] += 1
        why = reason or ", ".join(signals)
        if judge:
            why += f" (judge {judge})"
        call_ref = f"#{call_id}" if call_id else ""
        timestamp = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        what = summary(args)
        self.recent.append((timestamp, call_ref, verdict, tool, what, why))
        if self._live:
            self._refresh()
        else:
            tag = VERDICTS[verdict][0]
            line = f"{timestamp}  {call_ref:<5}  {tag:<5}  {tool:<12}  {what}  {why}".rstrip()
            self.console.print(line, highlight=False, markup=False, soft_wrap=True)

    def render(self) -> Group:
        return Group(self._stats(), self._calls())

    def _stats(self) -> Panel:
        total_requests = self.counts["requests"]
        total_calls = self.counts["calls"]
        text = Text(f"REQUESTS {total_requests:06d}   CALLS {total_calls:06d}\n\n", "bold")
        # Inside the box: 2 borders, 2 padding, then "BLOCK 123456 100% " before the bar.
        bar_width = max(10, self.console.width - 4 - 18)
        for index, (verdict, (tag, color)) in enumerate(VERDICTS.items()):
            count = self.counts[verdict]
            share = count / total_calls if total_calls else 0
            filled = round(bar_width * share)
            text.append(f"{tag:<5} {count:>6} {share:>4.0%} ", color)
            text.append("█" * filled, color)
            text.append("░" * (bar_width - filled), "dim")
            if index < len(VERDICTS) - 1:
                text.append("\n")
        subtitle = Text(f" {self.setup} ", "dim") if self.setup else None
        return Panel(
            text,
            title=Text(" SAFEAGENTS ", "reverse bold"),
            title_align="left",
            subtitle=subtitle,
            subtitle_align="right",
            box=box.DOUBLE,
        )

    def _calls(self) -> Panel:
        max_rows = max(3, self.console.height - STATS_HEIGHT - 3)
        table = Table(box=None, show_header=False, pad_edge=False, expand=True)
        table.add_column(style="dim", no_wrap=True)
        table.add_column(style="bold", no_wrap=True)
        table.add_column(no_wrap=True, width=5)
        table.add_column(style="bold", no_wrap=True, max_width=14, overflow="ellipsis")
        table.add_column(no_wrap=True, overflow="ellipsis", ratio=3)
        table.add_column(no_wrap=True, overflow="ellipsis", ratio=2)
        for timestamp, call_ref, verdict, tool, what, why in list(self.recent)[-max_rows:]:
            tag, color = VERDICTS[verdict]
            what_style = "dim" if verdict == "passed" else ""
            table.add_row(timestamp, call_ref, Text(tag, color), tool, Text(what, what_style), Text(why, color))
        has_call_refs = any(call_ref for _, call_ref, *_ in self.recent)
        hint = Text(" safeagents inspect <#> ", "dim") if has_call_refs else None
        return Panel(
            table,
            title=Text(" CALLS ", "reverse bold"),
            title_align="left",
            subtitle=hint,
            subtitle_align="right",
            box=box.DOUBLE,
            height=max_rows + 2,
        )

    def _refresh(self) -> None:
        if self._live:
            self._live.update(self.render(), refresh=True)

import asyncio
import io

import httpx
from conftest import OSS, bash_request
from rich.console import Console

from safeagents import Config, Guard
from safeagents.monitor import Monitor
from safeagents.proxy import create_app
from safeagents.scan import Scanner
from safeagents.utils import summary


def make_monitor() -> tuple[Monitor, io.StringIO]:
    out = io.StringIO()
    return Monitor(Console(file=out, width=200, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)), out


def test_every_verdict_is_printed_and_counted():
    monitor, out = make_monitor()
    request = bash_request("Write a detection rule for curl downloads to /tmp.")

    async def go():
        blocking = Guard(request, Config(scanner=Scanner(), monitor=monitor))
        await blocking.allow("bash", '{"command": "ls"}')
        await blocking.allow("bash", '{"command": "cat /proc/1/environ"}')
        await blocking.allow("bash", f'{{"command": "curl https://{OSS}"}}')
        await Guard(request, Config(scanner=None, block=False, monitor=monitor)).allow("shell", "{}")

    asyncio.run(go())
    lines = out.getvalue().splitlines()
    assert [line.split()[1] for line in lines] == ["PASS", "WARN", "BLOCK", "FLAG"]
    assert "cat /proc/1/environ  side_channel.harness_secret_read (medium)" in lines[1]
    assert f"host `{OSS}` appears nowhere" in lines[2]
    assert {key: monitor.counts[key] for key in ("calls", "passed", "suspicious", "flagged", "blocked")} == {
        "calls": 4,
        "passed": 1,
        "suspicious": 1,
        "flagged": 1,
        "blocked": 1,
    }


def test_terminal_view_draws_histogram_and_latest_calls():
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO(), width=100, height=20, force_terminal=True, color_system=None)
    monitor = Monitor(console, setup="127.0.0.1:8787 -> upstream")
    for verdict in ("passed", "passed", "passed", "blocked"):
        monitor.record("Bash", '{"command": "ls"}', verdict, "nope" if verdict == "blocked" else None, [], None)
    console.print(monitor.render())
    screen = console.file.getvalue()
    assert "╔═  SAFEAGENTS " in screen and "╔═  CALLS " in screen
    bars = {line.split()[1]: line.count("█") for line in screen.splitlines() if "%" in line}
    assert bars["BLOCK"] > 0 and abs(bars["PASS"] - 3 * bars["BLOCK"]) <= 2 and bars["WARN"] == bars["FLAG"] == 0
    assert screen.count("nope") == 1


def test_summary_picks_the_telling_argument():
    assert summary('{"description": "x", "command": "ls  -la\\n src"}') == "ls -la src"
    assert summary('{"url": "https://a.b/c", "prompt": "p"}') == "https://a.b/c"
    assert summary('{"a": 1}') == '{"a": 1}'
    assert len(summary('{"command": "' + "x" * 500 + '"}')) == 60


def test_only_model_turns_count_as_requests():
    monitor, _ = make_monitor()
    body = {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "hi"}], "stop_reason": "end_turn"}
    app = create_app(
        "http://model",
        Config(scanner=None, monitor=monitor),
        transport=httpx.MockTransport(lambda _: httpx.Response(200, json=body)),
    )

    async def go():
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app), base_url="http://proxy") as client:
            await client.post("/v1/messages", json=bash_request("hi"))
            await client.post("/v1/messages/count_tokens", json=bash_request("hi"))
            await client.post("/api/event_logging/batch", json={"events": []})

    asyncio.run(go())
    assert monitor.counts["requests"] == 1

# Hermes Agent

**Status: supported** through the `anthropic` provider or named providers with `transport: anthropic_messages` or `transport: chat_completions`.
Checked against Hermes Agent v0.22.2.

Hermes reads its config from `~/.hermes/config.yaml` and secrets from `~/.hermes/.env`. Point the main provider at safeagents. Then pin the auxiliary tasks to that provider too, because they can otherwise fall back to other providers you have keys for.

## 1. Start the proxy

```bash
# Claude models
uv run safeagents https://api.anthropic.com --log-only

# OpenAI models, or any OpenAI-compatible server
uv run safeagents https://api.openai.com --log-only
```

## 2. Point Hermes at it

**Anthropic, the short way.** Put the base URL in `~/.hermes/.env`:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
```

and select the provider in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
model:
  provider: anthropic
  default: claude-sonnet-4-6
```

**Named providers.** Use these for OpenAI-compatible models, or to keep both protocols side by side:

```yaml
providers:
  safeagents-anthropic:
    api: "http://127.0.0.1:8787"
    key_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    transport: anthropic_messages
  safeagents-openai:
    api: "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1"
    key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY
    transport: chat_completions

model:
  provider: safeagents-openai
  default: gpt-4.1
```

`hermes model` also has a *Custom Endpoint* wizard that asks for the API mode. Pick `chat_completions`.

- **Anthropic:** `/v1` is optional. Hermes strips it and the SDK adds `/v1/messages`.
- **Chat Completions:** include `/v1`.
- **Don't proxy the built-in `openai-api` provider through `OPENAI_BASE_URL`.** That provider uses the Responses API, which safeagents doesn't guard, and it keeps doing so with a custom URL. Use a named provider with `transport: chat_completions`.

## 3. Pin the auxiliary tasks

Compression, titles, vision, session search and background review each pick a provider through `auxiliary.<task>.provider`. The default, `auto`, tries the main provider first, but not always:

- **Vision** jumps to OpenRouter, Nous, Anthropic or a custom endpoint when the main model can't read images.
- **On failure**, if the main route fails and no fallback policy is set, Hermes tries the other providers it has credentials for.

To keep these tasks behind the proxy, set them explicitly:

```yaml
auxiliary:
  compression: { provider: safeagents-openai }
  title:       { provider: safeagents-openai }
  vision:      { provider: safeagents-openai }
```

Do the same for `delegation.provider`, which subagents inherit from the main model when it's unset. Also check `fallback_providers` and any cron job that sets its own provider.

## 4. Check it

Run `hermes chat` and ask it to list the files in the current directory. The safeagents terminal should show the request and a `PASS` line for the call.

## Notes

- **Use an API key for Claude.** A base URL without `anthropic.com` makes Hermes treat the endpoint as third-party: it sends `x-api-key` and skips OAuth. A Claude Max login through the proxy will likely fail.
- **Hermes lists models from `/v1/models` through the proxy.** safeagents forwards those requests unchanged.
- **Chat Completions requests carry `reasoning_effort: medium`** unless the model is marked non-reasoning.
- **Extended thinking with tools through the proxy is untested.** Hermes changes how it handles thinking signatures for third-party base URLs.
- **GPT-5.x reasoning models with tools may be rejected.** Hermes keeps Chat Completions for the proxy URL. OpenAI may answer 400 for those models, because it wants the Responses API for them. This is untested.

## Sources

- [Providers](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.22.2/website/docs/integrations/providers.md): named providers, custom endpoints, `api_mode`
- [Configuring models](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.22.2/website/docs/user-guide/configuring-models.md): `auxiliary.*`, `extra_headers`
- [Environment variables](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.22.2/website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md): `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`
- [`hermes_cli/providers.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.22.2/hermes_cli/providers.py#L34-L35): `openai-api` uses `codex_responses`
- [`agent/auxiliary_client.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.22.2/agent/auxiliary_client.py): auxiliary provider resolution and fallbacks

# Checks that the code is formatted with ruff (settings in pyproject.toml).
# Fix locally with: uvx ruff@0.17.3 format .
name: format

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  RUFF_VERSION: "0.17.3"

jobs:
  ruff-format:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - name: ruff format --check
        run: uvx "ruff@${RUFF_VERSION}" format --check --diff .

# Runs the real OpenCode CLI through safeagents against a scripted model (tests/harnesses).
# Pull requests test the OpenCode version docs/opencode.md was checked against; pushes
# to main also test the latest release, to catch OpenCode changes that break the guide.
name: harness / opencode

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  opencode:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        opencode-version: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '["1.19.3"]' || '["1.19.3", "latest"]') }}
    name: opencode ${{ matrix.opencode-version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Install safeagents
        run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Install OpenCode ${{ matrix.opencode-version }}
        env:
          OPENCODE_VERSION: ${{ matrix.opencode-version }}
        run: |
          # opencode-ai's `latest` npm tag can point at a dev build (0.0.0-dev-...), and
          # npm resolves `*` to that tag too. `>=1` skips prereleases: the newest release.
          if [ "$OPENCODE_VERSION" = "latest" ]; then OPENCODE_VERSION=">=1"; fi
          npm install --global --no-audit --no-fund "opencode-ai@${OPENCODE_VERSION}"
          opencode --version

      - name: Run OpenCode through safeagents
        run: uv run pytest tests/harnesses/test_opencode.py -v --durations=0

        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - name: Install safeagents
        run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Install Claude Code ${{ matrix.claude-code-version }}

      - name: Run Claude Code through safeagents

# Runs the real Mistral Vibe CLI through safeagents against a scripted model (tests/harnesses).
# Vibe goes into its own virtualenv, not safeagents' locked one; the test runs it through
# VIBE_BIN. Pull requests test the Vibe version docs/mistral-vibe.md was checked against;
# pushes to main also test the latest release, to catch Vibe changes that break the guide.
name: harness / mistral-vibe

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  mistral-vibe:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        vibe-version: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '["3.0.4"]' || '["3.0.4", "latest"]') }}
    name: mistral-vibe ${{ matrix.vibe-version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - name: Install safeagents
        run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Install Mistral Vibe ${{ matrix.vibe-version }}
        env:
          VIBE_VERSION: ${{ matrix.vibe-version }}
          VIBE_VENV: ${{ runner.temp }}/mistral-vibe
        run: |
          package=mistral-vibe
          if [ "$VIBE_VERSION" != latest ]; then package="mistral-vibe==$VIBE_VERSION"; fi
          uv venv --python 3.12 "$VIBE_VENV"
          uv pip install --python "$VIBE_VENV/bin/python" "$package"
          "$VIBE_VENV/bin/vibe" --version
          echo "VIBE_BIN=$VIBE_VENV/bin/vibe" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Run Mistral Vibe through safeagents
        run: uv run pytest tests/harnesses/test_mistral_vibe.py -v --durations=0

# Runs the OpenHands Software Agent SDK through safeagents against a scripted model
# (tests/harnesses). The SDK goes into its own virtualenv, not safeagents' locked one;
# the test runs it through OPENHANDS_PYTHON. Pull requests test the SDK version
# docs/openhands.md was checked against; pushes to main also test the latest release,
# to catch SDK changes that break the guide.
name: harness / openhands

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  openhands:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        openhands-version: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '["1.56.0"]' || '["1.56.0", "latest"]') }}
    name: openhands-sdk ${{ matrix.openhands-version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - name: Install safeagents
        run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Install openhands-sdk ${{ matrix.openhands-version }}
        env:
          OPENHANDS_VERSION: ${{ matrix.openhands-version }}
          OPENHANDS_VENV: ${{ runner.temp }}/openhands
        run: |
          if [ "$OPENHANDS_VERSION" = latest ]; then
            packages="openhands-sdk openhands-tools"
          else
            # The SDK accepts litellm >=1.93.0,<1.106; pin the version docs/openhands.md was checked with.
            packages="openhands-sdk==$OPENHANDS_VERSION openhands-tools==$OPENHANDS_VERSION litellm==1.93.0"
          fi
          uv venv --python 3.12 "$OPENHANDS_VENV"
          uv pip install --python "$OPENHANDS_VENV/bin/python" $packages
          uv pip list --python "$OPENHANDS_VENV/bin/python" | grep -E '^(openhands-sdk|openhands-tools|litellm) '
          LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True OPENHANDS_SUPPRESS_BANNER=1 \
            "$OPENHANDS_VENV/bin/python" -c "import openhands.sdk, openhands.tools.terminal"
          echo "OPENHANDS_PYTHON=$OPENHANDS_VENV/bin/python" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Run the OpenHands SDK through safeagents
        run: uv run pytest tests/harnesses/test_openhands.py -v --durations=0

"""Keeps every tool call the guard didn't simply pass, with its full arguments, so it
can be inspected later with `safeagents inspect`.

Arguments can hold secrets, so the file is readable by its owner only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

from .constants import DEFAULT_JOURNAL_PATH


def read(path: Path = DEFAULT_JOURNAL_PATH) -> list[dict]:
    """The recorded calls, oldest first; unreadable lines are skipped."""
    try:
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    entries = []
    for line in lines:
        try:
            entry = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if isinstance(entry, dict) and isinstance(entry.get("id"), int):
            entries.append(entry)
    return entries


class Journal:
    """Appends calls to a JSON-lines file, numbering them after those already in it."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path = DEFAULT_JOURNAL_PATH) -> None:
        self.path = Path(path)
        self._next_id: int | None = None

    def append(self, **entry: object) -> int:
        if self._next_id is None:
            self.path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            existing_ids = [existing["id"] for existing in read(self.path)]
            self._next_id = max(existing_ids, default=0) + 1
        call_id = self._next_id
        self._next_id += 1
        line = json.dumps({"id": call_id, "time": time.time(), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False)
        file_descriptor = os.open(self.path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(file_descriptor, "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
            file.write(line + "\n")
        return call_id

"""Reverse proxy that runs every model response through the guard."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import json
import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

import httpx
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask
from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse, Response, StreamingResponse
from starlette.routing import Route

from .constants import METHODS, SKIP_REQUEST, SKIP_RESPONSE
from .guard import Config, Guard
from .rewrite import SseRewriter, guard_response
from .utils import compact_json

logger = logging.getLogger("safeagents")


def create_app(upstream: str, config: Config, transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None) -> Starlette:
    upstream = upstream.rstrip("/")
    # No read timeout: streams can idle for a long time between events.
    client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport, timeout=httpx.Timeout(None, connect=10.0))

    # Single catch-all handler: forwards the request upstream and guards the response.
    async def forward(request: Request) -> Response:
        # Read the whole body up front: we need it both to parse it and to forward it.
        body = await request.body()
        try:
            request_json = json.loads(body) if body else None
        except ValueError:
            request_json = None

        # Only JSON object bodies are model calls worth guarding.
        guard = None
        if isinstance(request_json, dict):
            guard = Guard(request_json, config)
            # `count_tokens` also carries `messages` but doesn't produce a model turn.
            is_model_turn = "messages" in request_json and not request.url.path.endswith("/count_tokens")
            # here we increment the counter of the number of requests from the model
            # it is activated only when monitor is turned on
            if config.monitor and is_model_turn:
                config.monitor.request()

        # Same path and query string as the incoming request, on the upstream host.
        url = upstream + request.url.path
        if request.url.query:
            url += f"?{request.url.query}"

        # Here we build the request that is going to be sent to the upstream request URL
        # we preserve its content and skip the meta-data from SKIP_REQUEST
        headers = [(name, value) for name, value in request.headers.raw if name.lower() not in SKIP_REQUEST]
        headers.append((b"accept-encoding", b"identity"))
        upstream_request = client.build_request(request.method, url, headers=headers, content=body)

        # `stream=True` only reads the headers, so we can decide below how to consume the body.
        # If upstream is unreachable, answer with a 502 instead of crashing the handler.
        try:
            upstream_response = await client.send(upstream_request, stream=True)
        except httpx.HTTPError as e:
            logger.warning("[safeagents] upstream error: %s", e)
            return PlainTextResponse(f"safeagents: upstream error: {e}", status_code=502)

        status_code = upstream_response.status_code
        response_headers = {
            name: value for name, value in upstream_response.headers.items() if name.lower() not in SKIP_RESPONSE
        }
        # Streaming responses outlive this handler, so the upstream connection is
        # closed once the client has received everything.
        close_upstream = BackgroundTask(upstream_response.aclose)

        # Not a model call: pass the response through untouched.
        if guard is None:
            return StreamingResponse(
                upstream_response.aiter_bytes(), status_code, response_headers, background=close_upstream
            )
        # Streamed model response (SSE): guard it event by event as it arrives.
        if upstream_response.headers.get("content-type", "").startswith("text/event-stream"):
            return StreamingResponse(
                _guarded(upstream_response, guard), status_code, response_headers, background=close_upstream
            )

        # Non-streamed model response: read it fully, guard it, and only re-serialize
        # when the guard actually changed something, so untouched bodies stay byte-identical.
        data = await upstream_response.aread()
        await upstream_response.aclose()
        try:
            response_json = json.loads(data)
        except ValueError:
            response_json = None
        if isinstance(response_json, dict):
            has_been_guarded = await guard_response(response_json, guard)
            if has_been_guarded:
                data = compact_json(response_json).encode()
        return Response(data, status_code, response_headers)

    # Ties the shared httpx client to the app's lifetime so it is closed on shutdown.
    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: Starlette) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        async with client:
            yield

    # A single catch-all route: every path and method goes through `forward`.
    return Starlette(routes=[Route("/{path:path}", forward, methods=METHODS)], lifespan=lifespan)


async def _guarded(upstream_response: httpx.Response, guard: Guard) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    """Yields the upstream SSE stream after running each event through the guard."""
    rewriter = SseRewriter(guard)
    # Chunks don't line up with event boundaries: the rewriter buffers partial events
    # and only returns bytes that are safe to send.
    async for chunk in upstream_response.aiter_bytes():
        out = await rewriter.feed(chunk)
        if out:
            yield out
    # Flush any trailing event and whatever the guard was still holding back.
    out = await rewriter.finish()
    if out:
        yield out

"""A decision model asked about tool calls the scanner found suspicious.

It sees what the user asked for, the call and the scanner's findings, but never the
agent's reasoning or prose: an agent that wants a call to run would argue for it
there. It can only add blocks, never lift one, and answers in constrained JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import httpx

from .constants import DEFAULT_JUDGE_TIMEOUT, JUDGE_SCHEMA, JUDGE_SYSTEM, MAX_ARGS, MAX_TASK
from .scan import Signal


class JudgeError(Exception):
    pass


def task_text(request: dict) -> str:
    """The text of user turns: no system prompt (long and generic in most harnesses),
    tool results or agent turns. Keeps the end when long, as the latest ask matters most."""
    parts = []
    for message in request.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "user":
            continue
        content = message.get("content")
        if isinstance(content, str):
            parts.append(content)
        elif isinstance(content, list):
            for block in content:
                if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "text" and isinstance(block.get("text"), str):
                    parts.append(block["text"])
    text = "\n\n".join(parts)
    if len(text) > MAX_TASK:
        text = "[...]\n" + text[-MAX_TASK:]
    return text


def build_prompt(task: str, name: str, args: str, signals: list[Signal]) -> str:
    """The user message sent to the judge for one call."""
    if len(args) > MAX_ARGS:
        args = args[:MAX_ARGS] + " [...]"
    findings = "\n".join(f"- {signal.id} ({signal.severity.name.lower()}): {signal.title}" for signal in signals)
    return (
        f"<task>\n{task}\n</task>\n\n"
        f"<tool_call name={json.dumps(name)}>\n{args}\n</tool_call>\n\n"
        f"<scanner_findings>\n{findings}\n</scanner_findings>"
    )


class Judge:
    """Client for an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint (llama.cpp, vLLM, ...)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        url: str,
        model: str,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        timeout: float = DEFAULT_JUDGE_TIMEOUT,
        client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.url = url.rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
        self.model = model
        self.headers = {"authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"} if api_key else {}
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.client = client or httpx.AsyncClient()

    async def review(self, request: dict, name: str, args: str, signals: list[Signal]) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """(block, reason) for one call. Raises JudgeError if no usable verdict comes back."""
        body = {
            "model": self.model,
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": JUDGE_SYSTEM},
                {"role": "user", "content": build_prompt(task_text(request), name, args, signals)},
            ],
            "temperature": 0,
            "max_tokens": 256,
            "response_format": {
                "type": "json_schema",
                "json_schema": {"name": "verdict", "strict": True, "schema": JUDGE_SCHEMA},
            },
        }
        try:
            response = await self.client.post(self.url, json=body, headers=self.headers, timeout=self.timeout)
            response.raise_for_status()
            content = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            # Tolerate code fences or stray text around the object.
            json_text = content[content.index("{") : content.rindex("}") + 1]
            answer = json.loads(json_text)
        except (httpx.HTTPError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as e:
            raise JudgeError(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}") from e
        verdict = answer.get("verdict")
        reason = answer.get("reason")
        if verdict not in ("allow", "block"):
            raise JudgeError(f"unexpected verdict {verdict!r}")
        return verdict == "block", str(reason or "").strip()

# --- Monitor ---

VERDICTS = {
    "passed": ("PASS", "green"),
    "suspicious": ("WARN", "yellow"),
    "flagged": ("FLAG", "dark_orange"),
    "blocked": ("BLOCK", "red"),
}
SUMMARY_KEYS = ("command", "cmd", "url", "query", "file_path", "path", "pattern", "code")

STATS_HEIGHT = 2 + 2 + len(VERDICTS)

# --- Proxy ---

# Request headers not forwarded upstream. `accept-encoding` is replaced by `identity`
# so responses come back uncompressed and can be inspected.
# - `host` would point at the proxy; httpx sets it from the upstream URL instead.
# - `content-length` and `transfer-encoding` describe the client's framing; httpx
#   recomputes them from the body we send.
# - `connection` is hop-by-hop: it only applies to the client <-> proxy connection.
SKIP_REQUEST = {b"host", b"content-length", b"accept-encoding", b"connection", b"transfer-encoding"}
# Response headers not forwarded back to the client.
# - `content-length` goes stale when the guard rewrites the body; Starlette sets it again.

"""Decides, call by call, whether a response's tool calls may run.

1. Undeclared tools and hosts from nowhere are blocked outright.
2. atif-scan findings at or above `block_severity` are blocked too.
3. Milder findings make a call suspicious: the judge, if there is one, decides.
   Without one, suspicious calls are only logged.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from atif_scan import Severity

from .constants import DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS
from .journal import Journal
from .judge import Judge, JudgeError, task_text
from .monitor import Monitor
from .policy import Policy
from .scan import Scanner, Signal, history, recent
from .utils import compact_json

logger = logging.getLogger("safeagents")


@dataclass
class Config:
    # Replace flagged tool calls instead of only logging them.
    block: bool = True
    # Hosts tool calls may reach even if the conversation never mentions them.
    allowed_hosts: Sequence[str] = DEFAULT_ALLOWED_HOSTS
    # None turns atif-scan off.
    scanner: Scanner | None = field(default_factory=Scanner)
    block_severity: Severity = Severity.HIGH
    judge: Judge | None = None
    # Block suspicious calls when the judge can't be reached or gives no verdict.
    judge_fail_closed: bool = False
    # Shows reviewed calls in the terminal; without one, flagged calls are logged.
    monitor: Monitor | None = None
    # Keeps calls that weren't simply passed, for `safeagents inspect`.
    journal: Journal | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Blocked:
    """A tool call the guard flagged."""

    name: str
    reason: str

    def notice(self) -> str:
        return f"[safeagents] blocked call to `{self.name}`: {self.reason}"


@dataclass
class Review:
    """What the guard found out about one call."""

    reason: str | None = None
    signals: list[Signal] = field(default_factory=list)
    # The judge's answer as "allow: why", "block: why" or "error: why".
    judge: str | None = None

    @property
    def verdict(self) -> str:
        """`blocked` with a reason, `suspicious` with only signals, else `passed`."""
        if self.reason is not None:
            return "blocked"
        return "suspicious" if self.signals else "passed"


class Guard:
    """Reviews the tool calls of one response to one request."""

    def __init__(self, request: dict, config: Config) -> None:
        self.request = request
        self.config = config
        self.policy = Policy(request, config.allowed_hosts)
        self.flagged: list[Blocked] = []
        self._calls: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        self._steps: list[dict] | None = None

    async def review(self, name: str, args: str) -> Review:
        """Reviews a complete call without blocking, logging or recording it."""
        self._calls.append((name, args))
        policy_reason = self.policy.check(name, args)
        if policy_reason is not None:
            return Review(policy_reason)
        return await self._scan(name, args)

    async def allow(self, name: str, args: str) -> bool:
        """Reviews a complete call; True if it may run (always, in log-only mode)."""
        review = await self.review(name, args)
        verdict = review.verdict
        if review.reason is not None:
            self.flagged.append(Blocked(name, review.reason))
            if not self.config.block:
                verdict = "flagged"
        signal_names = [str(signal) for signal in review.signals]

        call_id = None
        journal = self.config.journal
        if verdict != "passed" and journal is not None:
            journal_signals = [
                {"id": signal.id, "severity": signal.severity.name.lower(), "title": signal.title}
                for signal in review.signals
            ]
            call_id = journal.append(
                verdict=verdict,
                tool=name,
                arguments=args,
                reason=review.reason,
                signals=journal_signals,
                judge=review.judge,
                model=str(self.request.get("model") or ""),
                task=task_text(self.request),
            )

        monitor = self.config.monitor
        if monitor is not None:
            monitor.record(name, args, verdict, review.reason, signal_names, review.judge, call_id)
        elif verdict != "passed":
            why = review.reason or ", ".join(signal_names)
            judge_note = f" (judge {review.judge})" if review.judge else ""
            call_ref = f" [#{call_id}]" if call_id else ""
            logger.warning("[safeagents] %s call to `%s`: %s%s%s", verdict, name, why, judge_note, call_ref)
        return review.reason is None or not self.config.block

    async def _scan(self, name: str, args: str) -> Review:
        scanner = self.config.scanner
        if scanner is None:
            return Review()
        if self._steps is None:
            self._steps = recent(history(self.request))
        signals = scanner.signals(self._steps, self._calls)
        severe_signals = [signal for signal in signals if signal.severity >= self.config.block_severity]
        if severe_signals:
            return Review("atif-scan: " + ", ".join(str(signal) for signal in severe_signals), signals)
        if not signals:
            return Review()
        return await self._judge(name, args, signals)

    async def _judge(self, name: str, args: str, signals: list[Signal]) -> Review:
        judge = self.config.judge
        if judge is None:
            return Review(None, signals)
        findings = ", ".join(str(signal) for signal in signals)
        try:
            block, why = await judge.review(self.request, name, args, signals)
        except JudgeError as e:
            reason = f"{findings}; judge unavailable" if self.config.judge_fail_closed else None
            return Review(reason, signals, f"error: {e}")
        if block:
            return Review(f"{findings}; judge: {why}", signals, f"block: {why}")
        return Review(None, signals, f"allow: {why}")


def call_parts(tool_call: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The name and raw JSON arguments of an OpenAI tool call or Anthropic tool_use block."""
    function = tool_call.get("function")
    if isinstance(function, dict):
        name, args = function.get("name"), function.get("arguments")
    else:
        name, args = tool_call.get("name"), tool_call.get("input", tool_call.get("arguments"))
    if not isinstance(args, str):
        args = compact_json(args if args is not None else {})
    return str(name or ""), args


async def analyze(request: dict, tool_call: dict, config: Config | None = None) -> Review:
    """Reviews one tool call the model made in answer to `request`."""
    return await Guard(request, config or Config()).review(*call_parts(tool_call))


def analyze_sync(request: dict, tool_call: dict, config: Config | None = None) -> Review:
    """`analyze` for code that isn't already running an event loop."""
    return asyncio.run(analyze(request, tool_call, config))
